loops.title: A recording-chain peak is not a material identity
loops.question: Can a known-input complex ratio recover the total transfer while leaving its physical factorization ambiguous?
loops.finding: Total complex transfer is recovered to numerical precision; two distinct device/echo factorizations give exactly the same output.
limits: Known synthetic d permits a conditional echo calculation only
No physical apparatus recorded
Single-path labels and physical echo parameters are not identified by total H
Exact noiseless finite FIR exercise; no device, pressure, material or biological validation
loops.reviewedFinding: The noiseless known-FIR ratio recovers total transfer and predicts a held-out probe; exact alternative device/echo factorizations remain indistinguishable.

loops.title: Reference cancellation needs a stable, sensitive chain
loops.question: How do a near-notch and one-sample path change break reference division?
loops.finding: Reference division is exact only for the stable noiseless fixture; small path drift creates a false change, while regularization trades bounded noise for explicit bias.
limits: A .15 sensitivity mask is fixture-specific, not a universal physical stability threshold
Regularization bounds noise gain but adds bias
No room, object, microphone or speaker measured
Reference similarity flags changes but does not certify a stable physical chain
loops.reviewedFinding: Reference cancellation in the declared stable fixture is exact; a one-sample path change mimics an object change, while regularization bounds noise at the cost of calculable bias.

loops.title: Fit decay from a file, independently of strike gain
loops.question: Can one shared recording importer recover a declared single-mode decay from quantized WAV at different gains and phases?
loops.finding: The shared WAV importer and local fit recover the declared decay across gain/phase cases; silence and clipped recordings are rejected.
limits: actualbytes means generated and decoded PCM WAV, not a microphone recording
Local optimization depends on supplied nominal frequency and the declared single-mode model
Fitted decay describes the recorded channel, not intrinsic material damping
Quantization-only fixtures do not validate arbitrary device recordings
loops.reviewedFinding: One shared WAV importer/local fitter recovers the declared 500 Hz, 4 s^-1 decay across generated PCM gain/phase cases; silent and clipped files are rejected.

loops.title: A good decay fit can still describe recording gain
loops.question: Which model failures can residuals and window changes detect, and which remain exactly ambiguous?
loops.finding: Nearby modes and noise can raise residuals, but exponential recording gain is byte-identical to a different decay and passes the same fit checks.
limits: Generated WAV bytes are not recorded physical data
Residual/window checks can reject some failures but cannot certify intrinsic damping
Exact exponential gain is a counterexample, not a claimed universal AGC law
Multiple modal contributions, support and microphone dynamics remain physical alternatives
loops.reviewedFinding: The fixture detects overlapping modes through large residuals, but exponential gain and a different decay generate byte-identical recordings; a low residual cannot resolve that ambiguity.

loops.title: Preserve the original recording during analysis
loops.question: Can a versioned importer preserve source evidence while giving equivalent WAV and CSV analysis?
loops.finding: The protected version rejects source collisions, existing outputs, invalid CSV channel and symlink collisions while preserving equivalent valid WAV/CSV analysis.
limits: File integrity is not source authenticity or acoustic calibration
Original S2A/S2B fitter and results remain frozen
Low residuals retain the exact S2B physical ambiguity
User-supplied recording provenance is declared, not independently verified
loops.reviewedFinding: A versioned intake preserves raw files and existing outputs, rejects invalid CSV channels and source/symlink collisions, and gives identical decoded WAV/CSV traces.

loops.title: The time axis is a calibration premise
loops.question: Can identical samples yield different absolute decay and frequency under different clock labels?
loops.finding: A wrong timebase changes fitted frequency and decay together without changing samples; an independently known reference can correct this synthetic clock error.
limits: Generated PCM and timestamp fixtures are not a physical clock measurement
Independent reference frequency is an additional assumption; a same-clock generated tone is circular calibration
Header sample rate and reported device settings do not independently certify true sampling time
A constant reference tone reaches alpha0 search boundary; that flag is retained
loops.reviewedFinding: Identical samples give proportionally different absolute frequency and decay under a changed timebase; an independently known reference conditionally fixes the scale. The repaired timestamp test now exercises timestamp validation.

loops.title: A spatial magnitude map loses phase and direction
loops.question: What changes when a magnitude map is replaced by independent phase-referenced spatial samples?
loops.finding: Dense magnitude samples retain exact phase/direction ambiguities; two appropriately spaced complex samples recover the declared model coefficients with a shared phase reference.
limits: One-dimensional two-traveling-wave model is assumed, not a measured room
Conjugate-swap reverses larger traveling coefficient; known incident direction and passivity may exclude it
Complex samples require common phase reference; sequential phone recordings do not automatically provide one
Recovered coefficients do not identify material, source mechanism or three-dimensional boundaries
loops.reviewedFinding: Dense magnitude observations retain exact global-phase and conjugate-swap ambiguities; two quarter-wave-spaced complex samples recover coefficients only in the declared known-basis, shared-phase model.

loops.title: Spacing and a withheld position test the spatial inverse
loops.question: When does a second spatial sample add stable information, and can a withheld sample expose phase drift?
loops.finding: Near-degenerate spacing amplifies bounded noise; a two-point fit hides channel-specific phase drift that a withheld third point reveals.
limits: One-dimensional known-c model and common phase reference assumed
Half-wavelength singular cases are not inverted
A third sample can reject this mismatch but cannot certify every physical assumption
Noise direction is constructed worst case; not a phone error distribution
loops.reviewedFinding: Spatial inverse conditioning depends on separation; a two-point exact fit can hide channel phase drift while an independent withheld point exposes this declared mismatch.

loops.title: Counterbalance the household comparison before recording
loops.question: Does a balanced trial order remove a declared recording drift, and which condition-linked rival remains?
loops.finding: Balanced order cancels the declared linear recording drift in positive and null fixtures; a condition-linked gain rival remains byte-identical.
limits: All64trialWAVs and rival are generated fixtures, not spoon measurements
Fixed counterbalance cancels this linear order term, not arbitrary drift
Condition-linked nuisance is not removed by trial order
Public demo condition key is not blinded; future masked analysis requires separate custody
Recorded-channel contrast is not intrinsic material damping
loops.reviewedFinding: Balanced ABBA/BAAB order cancels the declared linear acquisition drift in positive and zero-effect generated tap fixtures; it does not distinguish an exactly equivalent condition-linked gain rival.

loops.title: Run the full plan and report every exclusion
loops.question: Can a strict batch workflow preserve evidence, align impacts, and withhold a primary result for an incomplete plan?
loops.finding: The complete planned set produces its synthetic recorded-channel contrast; missing, rejected or mismatched trials withhold the primary result while preserving all raw files.
limits: Complete dryrun is generated data, not an executed physical bench
Declared metadata and hashes establish neither authenticity nor physical calibration
Any surviving-trial contrast from an incomplete set is descriptive only
Recorded-channel effects retain the exact condition-linked gain rival fromS5A
No added research loop follows this final sound review
loops.reviewedFinding: The complete generated-file plan yields its declared recorded-channel contrast; impact alignment is exercised, raw files are preserved, and incomplete or malformed plans cannot produce a primary result.

empiricalBoundary: Generated simulations and WAV bytes only; no physical apparatus or participant measurements.
